Form, JSON and multipart args are not capped at all (bodyprocessors/urlencoded.go:27-30, json.go:31-35, multipart.go:117).

finding.guards_checked: Argument limit present on query args only; overflow is silent (no flag, no error returned to rules or connector); POST paths bypass the cap entirely. Not an enforced control for inspection completeness.

finding.claim: Content-Type matching for the URL-encoded body processor uses exact equality, so 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8' does not select the processor. ProcessRequestBody then skips body parsing, leaving ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY empty, unless a rule sets ctl:requestBodyProcessor=URLENCODED.
finding.source: Request header Content-Type with any parameter suffix (e.g. charset=UTF-8)
finding.sink: Body argument parsing skipped (ProcessRequestBody empty-processor branch) so ARGS_POST is never populated

finding.guards_checked: No fallback content-type detection; ForceRequestBodyVariable defaults false (waf.go:210). Compensation depends on the deployed ruleset setting ctl:requestBodyProcessor, which was not verified.

finding.claim: Multiple Content-Type headers: the body processor is chosen from the last matching header (each match overwrites reqbodyProcessor), while the MIME type passed to the processor is the first header (Get()[0]). A request with multipart/form-data first and application/x-www-form-urlencoded second is parsed as URL-encoded with no REQBODY_ERROR, so FILES/FILES_NAMES/MULTIPART_* are never populated.
finding.source: Two Content-Type request headers in order: multipart/form-data; boundary=X, then application/x-www-form-urlencoded
finding.sink: Body processing selection and parsing (ProcessRequestBody -> urlencoded ProcessRequest) without multipart inspection

finding.guards_checked: No duplicate-Content-Type rejection. Reverse order (urlencoded first, multipart second) fails in multipart.go:30-31 and sets REQBODY_ERROR, which is detectable. Severity depends on the backend choosing the first Content-Type header, which was not verified.

finding.claim: Multipart filename is stored raw (originFileName at line 58, filesCol.Add at line 99) with no path or trailing-slash normalization. Go's multipart.Part.FileName() applies filepath.Base, so an extension rule could miss 'shell.php/' while the backend saves 'shell.php'. Low confidence: backend behavior recalled from memory, not verified in this sandbox.
